newsitem.title: USA: Texaco sees 120,000bpd Eugene oil shut to end week.
newsitem.headline: Texaco sees 120,000bpd Eugene oil shut to end week.

text.p: Texaco Inc expects 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude to be shut in until Thursday at the earliest following a crack on part of its Eugene Island pipeline, which resulted in an oil spill on a lake in southern Louisiana.
The crack, discovered last Friday, was found on the final segement of the 155 mile line, which carries oil from offshore in the Gulf of Mexico to onshore storage terminals.

According to Texaco spokesman Pierre DeGruy, approximately 50,000 bpd of crude has been diverted away from the final 16-mile section which has been affected. But though the repair work has begun, 120,000 bpd will remain shut in until Thursday at the earliest.
He couldn't comment on whether force majeure would be declared on any shipments of crude oil because of the incident.

Meanwhile, a Coast Guard spokesman said the crude oil spill was larger than earlier thought and a ban on oyster harvesting in the northern part of Lake Barre, Terrebone, has been declared until assessments can be made.
"We've upped the estimate from 400 barrels to between 2,000 and 5,000 barrels, mostly as there are some deep pockets of oil trapped in the lake," the Coast Guard spokesman said.
The ban was issued by and is being administered by the Louisiana Health and Hospitals and the Fisheries and Wildlife Departments, he said.
